title: Hruday uniform local closeness of all AQ-type subsequential states and the boundary-independent first-order density
selection_reason: The AV1 lemma holds for every finite centered whole-star box, hence for every subsequential limit of the construction; two such limits are within 2D of each other on R in trace norm, and their first-order densities coincide. This is a quantitative boundary comparison, not uniqueness.
model: Zero-selected patterned family at both signs |tau|<=10^-8; two named construction families (centered whole-star boxes; boxes with all faces whose actual support is contained, per I1's padding prescription); local observable class B(H_R); trace norm on R; common clock.

parameters.topology: trace norm on fixed finite regions; norm on compact time windows for dynamics
parameters.constant: 2 D (AV1 admitted tier) for any two subsequential limits; first-order density rho^(1)_R explicit

required: 1. Prove (itemized, not by analogy) that both named families satisfy the AV1 premises: for the AQ1 centered whole-star boxes cite the admitted chain; for the I1 all-contained-face boxes with padding, prove the AM2 contraction at the same J_0 for the padded interaction family, the reset budget and the local trace-norm compactness. Name two topologies separately: trace norm on B(H_R) for states, and norm on compact time windows for dynamics.

2. Prove ||rho_R-rho'_R||_1<=2D for any two subsequential limits (same family or different families) at the same tau, with D the AV1 admitted tier; state that this is uniform local closeness, never uniqueness, whole-sequence convergence, translation invariance or a rate in N.

3. Derive the first-order reduced density rho^(1)_R explicitly from the AW1-admitted c^(1) as the R-marginal of -(c^(1) Omega_0^* + h.c.) restricted to the creations meeting R (forward), or from the derivative of the vacuum-overlap/fidelity identity (reverse); prove it is the same for every subsequential limit of either family; bound the second-order difference between two limits by 2 K_2' tau^2 with an explicit R-local K_2' built from the AW1 remainder items restricted to faces meeting R (not the whole-box K_2^+), and compare K_2' with K_2^+.

4. Give the mandatory sentence template (Jung loop-2 response) in the report and export the gate fields uniqueness_claimed:false, whole_sequence_claimed:false, rate_claimed:false, translation_invariance_claimed:false, boundary_independence_of_dynamics_claimed:false in results.json.

5. Controls: topology_named, two_families_named, subsequence_versus_whole_sequence, local_closeness_not_uniqueness, common_clock; a fixed-vector versus moving-vector example; a common enclosing interval is not equality; freeze; byte-identical replays.

6. Controls: 'uniform in N' must not be conflated with 'uniform in a'; the report defines 'quantitative boundary comparison' as a closeness bound plus a matching first-order term, explicitly not a variational statement about which boundary condition the infinite-volume theory selects.
claim_exclusions: whole-sequence convergence or a rate in N

preregistration.mandatory_sentence_template: For every pair of subsequential limits of the named construction families F1 and F2 at the same coupling, on the fixed cover R and for the frozen observable class, the reduced densities satisfy ||rho_R - rho'_R||_1 <= 2D and agree to first order in tau; this does not assert equality of the states, whole-sequence convergence, translation invariance, boundary independence of the dynamics, or a rate in N.

acceptance.accepted_within_scope: Both families verified, the closeness inequality and the first-order density proved by both routes with exact constants.
acceptance.limited: Closeness proved only for one family or without the first-order density.

direction_note: Paired as planned; the historical lens's sub-round-3 preference for single+skeptic is recorded as a dissent (the padding-family verification, the explicit first-order density and the R-local K_2' are new derivations).
